title: A Unified Framework of Graph Information Bottleneck for Robustness and Membership Privacy

problem.claim: Develop GNNs that are robust to adversarial attacks while preserving membership privacy.

gap.claim: Existing approaches generally do not simultaneously address robustness and membership privacy, while structural noise and limited labels complicate applying Information Bottleneck methods to graphs.

contributions.claim: A graph information bottleneck framework using a neighbor bottleneck to alleviate structural noise.
An optimization incorporating pseudo labels to reduce the prediction gap between labeled and unlabeled nodes for membership privacy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the studied problem and proposed graph information bottleneck framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Information Bottleneck can filter noisy information and regularize predictions on labeled samples, benefiting robustness and membership privacy.
Extensive experiments on real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate robust predictions and simultaneous preservation of membership privacy.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have achieved substantial success in modeling graph-structured data.
GNNs face adversarial attacks and membership inference attacks that can compromise predictions and training-data privacy.
Prior work generally treats robustness and membership privacy separately, motivating their joint consideration.
The framework combines a neighbor bottleneck for structural noise with pseudo-label optimization for membership privacy.
Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to show robust predictions and preserved membership privacy.

source_observation.claim: The framework jointly targets adversarial robustness and membership privacy.

interpretation.claim: When multiple security objectives are coupled, a shared information-control mechanism may address them together.

application.claim: For graph models deployed in sensitive domains, evaluate robustness and membership privacy as linked objectives rather than isolated properties.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the joint approach preserves performance across different graph structures, label regimes, or attack settings.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, attack settings, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The optimization procedure and model architecture are not described in detail.
No deployment, computational-cost, or reproducibility details are provided.
